examples.claim: Paper example uses 4 tokens per block; 7-token prompt maps logical blocks 0,1 to physical 7,1
examples.source: paper §4.3: 'The prompt has 7 tokens, so vLLM maps the first 2 logical KV blocks (0 and 1) to 2 physical KV blocks (7 and 1) ... stores the KV cache of the first 4 tokens in logical block 0 and the following 3 tokens in logical block 1'

examples.claim: Megatron-LM style tensor parallelism, SPMD, attention split on the head dimension
examples.source: paper §4.6: 'supporting the widely used Megatron-LM style tensor model parallelism ... SPMD ... the attention operator is split on the attention head dimension'

examples.claim: Beam k=4: blocks 0,1,3 shared by all; 6 by candidates 0 and 1; 7 by 2 and 3; 2,4,5,8 freed; 9-12 newly allocated
examples.source: paper §4.4: 'vLLM frees all physical blocks whose reference counts reach 0 (blocks 2, 4, 5, 8) ... allocates new physical blocks (blocks 9-12) ... all candidates share blocks 0, 1, 3; candidates 0 and 1 share block 6, and candidates 2 and 3 further share block 7'

examples.claim: --scheduling-policy fcfs|priority, default fcfs; priority: lower value first, ties by arrival
examples.source: vllm/config/scheduler.py: policy: SchedulerPolicy = 'fcfs'; '"priority" means requests are handled based on given priority (lower value means earlier handling) and time of arrival deciding any ties'

examples.claim: Swapping: no new requests until preempted sequences complete; CPU swap space bounded by GPU memory allocated for KV cache
examples.source: paper §4.5: 'stops accepting new requests until all preempted sequences are completed ... the swap space on the CPU RAM is bounded by the GPU memory allocated for the KV cache' (paper design; current V1 uses recompute, optimization.md)

examples.claim: Swap vs recompute: recompute constant across block sizes, swap poor for small blocks, comparable at block sizes 16-64
examples.source: paper §7.3: 'the overhead of recomputation remains constant across different block sizes ... For medium block sizes from 16 to 64, the two methods exhibit comparable end-to-end performance'

examples.claim: uv venv --python 3.12 --seed; uv pip install vllm --torch-backend=auto; vllm download-kernels
examples.source: quickstart.md L25-28 (same four lines); dry-run resolve succeeded (vllm 0.33.0)

examples.claim: TPU: uv pip install vllm-tpu; other accelerators via out-of-tree plugins following the Hardware-Pluggable RFC
examples.source: quickstart.md: 'you need to install the vllm-tpu package ... uv pip install vllm-tpu'; installation/README.md: 'third-party hardware plugins that live outside the main vllm repository. These follow the Hardware-Pluggable RFC'

examples.claim: Models come from Hugging Face by default; export VLLM_USE_MODELSCOPE=True before engine init for ModelScope
examples.source: quickstart.md: 'set the environment variable VLLM_USE_MODELSCOPE before initializing the engine ... export VLLM_USE_MODELSCOPE=True'

examples.claim: vllm CLI also has chat, complete, bench, run-batch, download-kernels
examples.source: docs/cli/README.md headings: serve, launch, chat, complete, bench, collect-env, download-kernels, run-batch, preload

examples.claim: Issue #7155: all available GPU memory allocated regardless of max_model_len; closed 'not planned' on 2024-12-04
examples.source: GitHub API: state closed, state_reason not_planned, closed_at 2024-12-04T02:07:23Z; body 'vLLM allocates all available GPU memory after loading model weights, regardless of the max_model_len setting'

examples.claim: --kv-offloading-size in GiB, default None (disabled), total across ranks when TP > 1
examples.source: vllm/config/cache.py: 'Size of the KV cache offloading buffer in GiB. When TP > 1, this is the total buffer size summed across all TP ranks. By default, this is set to None, which means no KV offloading is enabled'

examples.claim: CPU: x86 FP32/FP16/BF16; AArch64 NEON same types; Apple Silicon and IBM Z experimental; Python 3.11-3.14; vllm/vllm-openai-cpu image
examples.source: cpu.md 'Python: 3.11 -- 3.14'; cpu.x86.inc.md 'data types FP32, FP16 and BF16', 'docker pull vllm/vllm-openai-cpu:latest-x86_64'; cpu.arm.inc.md 'NEON, data types FP32, FP16 and BF16'; apple/s390x 'experimental support'

examples.claim: CPU --block-size multiples of 32, default 128; set dtype=bfloat16 if float16 misbehaves
examples.source: cpu.md: 'Use multiples of 32 as --block-size, which is 128 by default'; 'due to unstable float16 support in torch CPU, it is recommended to explicitly set dtype=bfloat16'

examples.claim: On the shown graph (same GPU, same length distribution) vLLM is 8.5-15x HF and 3.3-3.5x TGI
examples.source: blog: 'LLaMA-7B on an NVIDIA A10G GPU and LLaMA-13B on an NVIDIA A100 GPU (40GB) ... three parallel output completions. vLLM achieves 8.5x - 15x higher throughput than HF and 3.3x - 3.5x higher throughput than TGI'; the embedded image is perf_a100_n3 only, so the ranges span two settings, not one GPU

examples.claim: Alpaca + OPT-175B: large KV memory, short sequences, vLLM's advantage shrinks
examples.source: paper §6.2: 'vLLM's advantage over Orca (Oracle) and Orca (Pow2) is less pronounced ... OPT-175B allows for large GPU memory space available to store KV cache, while the Alpaca dataset has short sequences'
